It feeds the Schedule 511-B additions total behind Oklahoma AGI (Form 511 line 7) and therefore the line 9 figure calc.state_tax consumes; it does not touch treaty-exempt income (see treaty_note). Resolve via: 2024 Form 511 packet Schedule 511-A / Schedule 511-B instructions (the citation URL) for the bonus-depreciation add-back and its matching subtraction amounts; this pack ships no Schedule 511-A/B figures and calc.state_tax applies none.
_strings.@@c18557b38320: Treaty conformity — OK conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from OK income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the OK return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Oklahoma's resident return (Form 511) starts at line 1 from "Federal adjusted gross income (from Federal 1040 or 1040-SR)" and then applies Schedule 511-A (Oklahoma subtractions) and Schedule 511-B (Oklahoma additions) to arrive at Oklahoma AGI. The complete Schedule 511-B additions list for 2024 is closed and enumerated: (B1) state and municipal bond interest, (B2) out-of-state losses, (B3) lump-sum distributions not in federal AGI, (B4) federal net operating loss, (B5) recapture of depletion / excess federal depletion, (B6) recapture of Oklahoma 529 contributions, (B7) Oklahoma loss distributed by an electing PTE, (B8) Oklahoma bonus depreciation add-back (new for 2024), (B9) miscellaneous other additions. There is NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income anywhere in the 2024 resident packet (a full-text search of the packet for "treaty"/"treaties" returns zero hits). Because OK begins from federal AGI and does not add treaty income back (unlike CA Schedule CA), federally treaty-exempt income already excluded from federal AGI flows through and is NOT re-taxed by Oklahoma. Therefore conforms = true.

Must provide a copy of the federal return and, if applicable, the federal child care credit schedule. If Oklahoma AGI (line 7) is less than Federal AGI (line 1), compute on Schedule 511-F (prorated).

Tax line: Form 511, line 14(a): 'Oklahoma Income Tax from Tax Table (see pages 27-38 of instructions)', computed on line 13 'Oklahoma Taxable Income (line 9 minus line 12)', where line 12 = 'Total deductions and exemptions (add lines 10 and 11 or amount from Sch. 511-E, line 5)'. Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,000 — 'Special' additional $1,000 exemption per taxpayer/spouse who is 65 or older at the close of the tax year, allowed ONLY if Form 511 line 1 Federal AGI does not exceed: $15,000 single / $25,000 joint / $12,500 married filing separate / $19,000 head of household (2024 packet, Top of Form Instructions). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — if eligible, claim it in the exemption boxes at the top of Form 511 and it flows into line 11.); blind ($1,000 — Additional $1,000 exemption per taxpayer/spouse who is legally blind; part of the top-of-form exemption count flowing into Form 511 line 11. NOT applied by calc.state_tax — claim it on the form.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 CHANGE — MFJ/HOH/SURVIVING-SPOUSE TOP-TWO BRACKETS RE-INDEXED: the packet's What's New states 'Income levels are adjusted for the top two income tax rate brackets for income tax returns with a filing status of married filing joint, head of household or surviving spouse.' The 3.75% band widened from $9,800-$12,200 (2023) to $9,800-$14,400, so 4.75% now starts at $14,400; verified against BOTH the packet's $100,000+ worksheet constant (now $4,373; 2023: $4,395) and printed table rows spanning the old/new breakpoints (e.g. $12,200-$12,250 -> $225 = 2024 math, not 2023's $226; $14,400-$14,450 -> $308), AND 68 O.S. § 2355(C) 'For tax years 2024 and 2025' (3.75% on 'next $4,600.00'). Single/MFS brackets and all six rates (0.25%-4.75%) are unchanged from 2023. Base guidance: Supply 2024 Form 511, line 9 'Oklahoma income after adjustments (line 7 minus line 8)'. Line 1 starts from federal AGI; lines 2-8 apply Oklahoma subtractions (Schedule 511-A), out-of-state income (line 4), Oklahoma additions (Schedule 511-B) and Oklahoma adjustments (Schedule 511-C) to reach line 9. The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Form 511 line 10) and $1,000 per exemption/dependent (Form 511 line 11) to reproduce line 13 'Oklahoma Taxable Income', and applies the brackets to reproduce line 14a. Do NOT pre-subtract deductions or exemptions from the figure you supply. If Form 511 line 4 (out-of-state income) is more than zero, or you itemize, the shipped fixed deduction/exemption amounts do not apply — see notes. Tax Table mandate below $100,000: Form 511 line 14a instructs 'Oklahoma Income Tax from Tax Table (see pages 27-38 of instructions)'. The table's $50-wide bands compute tax at the band midpoint, so plain bracket math may differ from the table by a few dollars within a band. The filed form must use the table below $100,000. Taxable income of $100,000 or more uses the packet's worksheets (p. 38): Single/MFS tax = $4,562 plus 0.0475 of the excess over $100,000; MFJ/HOH/Qualified Widow(er) tax = $4,373 plus 0.0475 of the excess over $100,000. Printed worksheet constants vs exact bracket sums (re-derived for 2024): the MFJ/HOH/QW constant $4,373 exactly equals the cumulative bracket sum at $100,000 ($307.00 through $14,400, plus 4.75% x $85,600 = $4,066); the Single/MFS constant $4,562 is the exact cumulative sum $4,561.50 rounded up $0.50, so above $100,000 the Single/MFS form worksheet can come out $1 higher than exact marginal bracket math after whole-dollar rounding. Bracket schedule source: the 2024 Form 511 packet prints only the Tax Table and the $100,000+ worksheets, not a marginal rate schedule. The brackets shipped here are copied verbatim from 68 O.S. § 2355(C) as in force for tax years 2024 and 2025 (current OSCN text, https://www.oscn.net/applications/oscn/DeliverDocument.asp?CiteID=92565 — the Oklahoma State Courts Network is the state courts' official statute publisher). Every bracket boundary was cross-checked against the packet's printed table rows and worksheet constants. NOTE for future maintainers: subsection D of the same section prints a DIFFERENT schedule 'For tax year 2026 and for subsequent tax years' (0%/2.5%/3.5%/4.5%) — do not use it for 2024/2025. One schedule covers Single and Married Filing Separately (identical thresholds — 68 O.S. § 2355(C)(1)); a second schedule covers Married Filing Jointly, surviving spouse, AND Head of Household (68 O.S. § 2355(C)(2)) — HOH is NOT a separate schedule; it is duplicated from MFJ here. The tax table likewise has only two columns: 'Single or married filing separate' and 'Married filing joint or head of household'. Qualifying surviving spouse uses the married-filing-jointly column and schedule (2024 tax table footnote: 'This column must also be used by a Qualified Surviving Spouse'; the statute includes surviving spouses in the MFJ paragraph; the line 10 instructions give QSS the $12,700 standard deduction) — the engine's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping is correct for Oklahoma. Out-of-state income gate: if Form 511 line 4 (out-of-state income, except wages) is more than zero, do NOT complete lines 10-11 — Schedule 511-E prorates deductions and exemptions instead, so the fixed standard deduction and $1,000 exemptions shipped here do not apply; compute on the form. Itemizers: if you claimed itemized deductions on your federal return you MUST claim Oklahoma itemized deductions (Schedule 511-D) instead of the standard deduction; Oklahoma itemized deductions are capped at $17,000 (charitable contributions and medical expenses are not subject to the cap). The shipped standard deduction applies only to federal standard-deduction claimants. You qualify for the Oklahoma standard deduction even when claimed as a dependent on another return. Form 511 line 14b add-ons are NOT modeled: the additional 10% tax on nonqualified Health Savings Account withdrawals, recapture of the Oklahoma Affordable Housing Tax Credit, and IRC Section 965(h) installment payments. Farm Income Averaging (Form 573, entered on line 14a with a '1' in the box) is also not modeled. Oklahoma's personal/dependent allowances are true income-base exemptions (Form 511 line 11 is subtracted from income before the rate applies via lines 12-13), not tax credits. Separately, Oklahoma's Child Care/Child Tax Credit (line 15, Schedule 511-F), Oklahoma EIC (line 28, Schedule 511-G, 5% of the federal EIC under 2020 rules), Sales Tax Relief Credit (line 25, Form 538-S, $40/exemption), Property Tax Relief credit (line 24, Form 538-H), and the NEW-for-2024 Parental Choice Tax Credit for Homeschool Expenses (line 29, Form 591-D) are CREDITS against tax and are not part of this computation. All Form 511 money entries are whole dollars ('00' boxes); the packet's rounding rule ('$2.50 to $2.99 - round up to $3.00') matches the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars.
